title: Liverpool vs. Man City Player Ratings: Premier League’s Villains Embrace Their Role
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack1:48 PM EDTMan City took full advantage of Ryan Gravenberch’s red card.  / Michael Regan/Getty ImagesManchester City ran amok after Ryan Gravenberch was shown a second yellow card on the hour of Sunday’s eagerly anticipated Premier League clash at Anfield, with superb goals from Erling Haaland, Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki seeing the visitors home.

The Cityzens were, of course, in action for the first time since an independent comission ruled that the club were guilty on almost all counts of serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations.

A hostile, bitter Anfield thus met the defiant visitors, who were aiming to respond to Arsenal’s come-from-behind victory against Leeds United. And while many will question the significance of these points in the long run, there’s no denying that City’s response was emphatic.

It was control versus chaos, and Maresca’s facilitation of the former won out on Merseyside. Liverpool were bright enough but hindered by key absences, particularly in attack. They offered plenty of bark but little bite, and City made them pay after Gravenberch’s dismissal.

The Reds collapsed, in truth, but City’s goals were of the highest quality. Within six minutes of Gravenberch solemnly strolling down the tunnel, strikes from Haaland and Doku handed Maresca’s side a 2–0 lead. Cherki’s goal 13 minutes later was typical of the Frenchman, and wrapped up the perfect day out for the almost-universally resented Cityzens.

Anfield was vociferous in its reproach of the visitors. / Alex Pantling/Getty ImagesThis was the fixture the soccer world had waited ever so patiently for since Manchester City’s guilty verdict came to light two weeks ago. A trip to Anfield just had to be on the horizon, didn’t it?

The extent of City’s financial doping has brought the sport, particularly the Premier League, into disrepute, with its consequences catastrophically far-reaching. Liverpool have every right to feel most aggrieved, given that the number of duels lost to Pep Guardiola’s Cityzens during Jürgen Klopp’s reign.

And this was the first meeting between the two clubs without either of the aforementioned managers in over a decade. In truth, the on-field action almost felt secondary. Much of the intrigue surrounding the pre-match histrionics and Anfield’s reaction to the great injustice.

Evasive action was taken by the visitors, who took an unfamiliar route to the ground and were keen to offer their show of defiance. Supporters ’Poznan-d’ in the face of “You’ll Never Walk Alone,” booed the Premier League anthem and waved inflatable bananas in homage to bleaker times in a pre-Premier League world. They’re victims in all this, too; but on Merseyside, they sided with those boasting the “irrefutable evidence” that’s yet to come to light.

And ultimately, Enzo Maresca’s side would prove that, despite the animosity, they remain an excellent soccer team. Fans will relish the short-term glee, but the majority will wonder what this all means
Lewis Koumas led Liverpool’s attack. / Paul ELLIS/AFP/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Alisson—4.9: There wasn’t all that much Liverpool’s goalkeeper could’ve done here. He was beaten by some outrageous quality from the away side.
RB: Ronald Araújo—6.5: Antoine Semenyo certainly felt he had the beating of the Barcelona loanee, who is proving a surprisingly valuable asset in the final third.
CB: Jérémy Jacquet—5.9: There were some masterful defensive sequences from the Frenchman, but City did have plenty of joy exploiting the channel Jacquet was supposed to be manning.

CB: Virgil van Dijk—5,8: Van Dijk was forced into a rather unfamiliar role due to City’s midfield overload. The Dutchman sought to quell this threat by stepping out of Liverpool’s defense and playing a key role in Iraola’s heavy man-to-man approach.
LB: Milos Kerkez—6.1: Ignored as an attacking outlet, and struggles to fill you with any confidence defensively.
CM: Ryan Gravenberch—6.5: This was Gravenberch of 2024–25... right up until he received a second yellow card just after the hour mark.
CM: Alexis Mac Allister—6.5: An up-and-down afternoon for Mac Allister, who scrapped around for the opening hour but struggled to offer any security thereafter.
RW: Víctor Muñoz—6.7: A real livewire who the Anfield faithful have quickly taken to. Nico O’Reilly had his work cut out all afternoon.
